transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you too. Um, I guess I came in because my mind is just constantly racing. I can't really get it to stop jumping from one thing to another. 

Like, I'll be worrying about whether our lab's new partnership is going to end up cutting my position, and then suddenly I'm stressing over whether all my data is wrong. And from there it just keeps going—worrying that my bills are going to pile up, or that my family thinks I'm falling behind everyone else. I even keep obsessing over whether I've already completely ruined my chances at getting into grad school. It's just a constant stream of things like that, all the time.

When you have these thoughts, do you feel like you are trying to resist them or push them away because they feel intrusive or distressing, or do you feel like you are just genuinely worried about these real-life situations?

I think I'm genuinely worried about those real-life things. They're actual situations I'm stressed about. But I do try to push them away sometimes just so I can get things done, though it doesn't really work. 

Like, I'll try to tell myself to just focus on one task, like finishing a lab report or checking an assay. But I can't control it. One worry just sets off another, and pretty soon I'm just staring at the screen while my head is running through every possible way things could go wrong.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your sleep, appetite, or overall energy levels since these worries started?

Yeah, my energy levels are definitely affected. Honestly, even after a full night in bed, I wake up feeling like I've already pulled an all-nighter. It's... it's just exhausting. 

And by the time I'm at work labeling samples, or even later when I'm just trying to cook dinner for my family, my body just feels so heavy. My brain feels completely drained. I haven't really noticed a huge change in my appetite or anything, but that feeling of just being totally wiped out is pretty constant.
Do you often find that your muscles feel tight, tense, or sore, particularly in your neck, shoulders, or jaw?

Yeah, actually. My shoulders and neck are just... they stay so tight during the day. I'll catch myself clenching my jaw while I'm looking over spreadsheets at work, and I don't even realize I'm doing it until it starts to hurt. By the time the evening rolls around, I usually have these headaches and my whole upper body is just stiff. It feels like I've been carrying heavy lab equipment around all day, even when I haven't been.
How long have you been experiencing these persistent worries and physical symptoms?

It's been about seven months now. It all started back when our lab went through a big funding shift and we brought on a new commercial partnership. That changed how everything was being run, and... yeah, that's when all this really kicked in.
